Nor a deuoish vit a clowd to fesh 'hem out o' te bottome o' te vayter. Tey drinke no bonny clabbe, i' fayt, now By my faters hand tey vill daunsh very vell. But tine owne Kingdomes. And goot men: tine owne shubshects. And te vfrow, ty daughter, that is in Tuchland. Pretee, sweet faysh doe. Nor beleeue no tayles, king YAMISH. No, nor forty, by my hand. Shtay te peepe i'sh come! harke, harke. Pre tee shee anoter daunsh and be not veary.
But tey musht eene come and daunch i'teyr mantels now; and snow tee how tey can foot te fading and te fadow, and te phip adunboyne I trow. I by S t . PATRICK vill tey; for tey be nimble men. For all tey haue no good vindsh to blow tem heter, nor ele mentsh to presherue 'hem. Tou hasht very good shubshects in Ireland. And vil runne t'rough fire, and vater for tee, ouer t • bog, and te Bannoke, be te graish o' got, and graish o' king, By got, tey vil fight for tee, king YAMISH, and for my mistresh tere. By creesh, tey vill shpend all teyr cowesh for tee. For, by got, tey loue tee in Ireland. Tey vill make tem shelues honesht. By my Lo. deputish hant not ten, in all ti great Britayne. Shall I call hem to tee? Let vsh daunsh ten. Daunsh DENNISE. How like tow tish YAMISH? And tey had fine cloyshs now, and liueries, like tine owne men and bee. I pre dee now, let not ty sweet faysht ladies make a mocke on 'hem, and scorne to daunsh vit'hem now, becash tey be poore. It ish better ten vsquebagh to daunsh vit PHATRICK. Nor all te foure cornersh o' te world, to creepe out on. Tey be honesht men. Tat loue ty mayesty heartily. Tey vill spend ter heart, in rer belly for tee, as vell as ter legs, in ter heelsh. Be not angry vit te honesh men, for te few rebelsh, & knauesh. Pray tee, bid 'hem velcome, and got make 'hem rish for tee. By iustish Delounes hant, not twenty. Tey shit like poore men i' the porsh yonder. A little till our mayshtersh be ready. But terugs make t'em shrug a little. Isht not pitty te cloysh be drown'd now?
And will leape ash light, be creesh saue me, ash he tat veareste biggesht fether in ty court, king YAMISH. A great good many, o'great goot shubshects. And my little mayshter. Pretee make mush on 'tem, Tou hasht not a hundret tousand sush men by my trote. By creesh sa' me I ha'forgot.
He may be of your rudenesse. Hold your tongues. And let your courser manners seeke some place, Fit for their wildnesse. This is none, be gone. Aduance, immortall Bard, come vp and view The glad, ding face of that great king, in whom So many prophecies of thine are knit. This is that IAMES of which long since thou sung'st, Should end our countreyes most vnnaturall broyles; And if her eare, then deafned with the drum, Would stoupe but to the musique of his peace, Shee need not with the spheares change harmony. This is the man thou promis'd should redeeme: If she would loue his counsels as his lawes, Her head from seruitude, her feete from fall, Her fame from barbarisme, her state from want, And in her all the fruits of blessing plant. Sing then some charme, made from his present lookes, That may assure thy former prophecies, And firme the hopes of these obedient spirits, Whose loue no lesse, then dutie hath cald forth Their willing powers: who if they had much more, Would doe their All, and thinke they could not moue Enough to honour that, which he doth loue. BOw both your heads at once, and hearts: Obedience doth not well in parts. It is but standing in his eye, You'll feele your selues chang'd by and by, Few liue, that know, how quick a spring Workes in the presence of a king: Tis done by this; your slough let fall, And come forth new-borne creatures all. SO breakes the sunne earths rugged chaines, Wherein rude winter bound her vaines; So growes both streame and source of price, That lately fetterd were with ice. So naked trees get crisped heads, And cullord coates the roughest meads, And all get vigour, youth, and spright, That are but look'd on by his light.
